newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Metals - China copper market seen tightening.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - China copper market seen tightening.

text.p: China's copper market will be tight in the coming months, with the Shanghai market seeing a possible squeeze in the short term, metals traders in Hong Kong and China said on Monday.
"The Shanghai market will become very interesting (over January, February and March), possibly seeing a squeeze," said a Beijing-based metals source.

Given the low domestic stocks available to the market, dwindling smelter inventories, China's possible exports and the scarce tonnages available from imports, the market would be very tight, other metals sources said.
All of the copper imported earlier was destined for state reserves, leaving very little in the market, traders said.
Already, it was hard to come across imported copper cathode in the marketplace, metals traders said.
"Even if you don't nominate brand and just ask for imports, it's very hard to come by and this is a very clear indication of the market situation," one trader said.

"We must also consider that the longs (in the Shanghai Metal Exchange) are going to take physical delivery out of the warehouses," the Beijing metals trader said, noting this would add to the tightness.
With the year-end coming up, Chinese companies would be squaring their books and December copper had ceased trading on the Shanghai Metal Exchange, some Chinese traders said.
Small-lot exports of copper continued as Chinese trading firms rushed to fulfill copper cathode re-export quotas in tolling as the year-end loomed, Hong Kong traders said.
"Either you re-export the material (from China) or you pay the full tax, which is too expensive," said one metals source.
"So we re-export the material, sell to someone who has other tolling contracts who will re-import it. They will buy from us in Hong Kong and bring it back to China," the copper trader said.
One copper smelter was heard concluding a contract to export about 2,000 tonnes of copper cathode in January on an FOB basis.
"The price at the moment is right to make exports profitable," said a source at the smelter. He declined to specify prices for the January contract.
"Foreigners are buying quite regularly. We've sold quite a lot of copper cathodes," the Chinese smelter source said, noting most of the material went to Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong.
China's physical demand had slowed down as the nation entered the traditionally slow season for trade and the markets were very dull, metals traders said.
Shanghai copper futures opened down on Monday, following the London Metal Exchange (LME) lead, but rose to 19,840 yuan ($2,390) per tonne in early trading.
Three-month copper on the LME finished Friday at $2,132 per tonne, down $26 from Thursday.
The latest Hong Kong indications of premium or discount in US$/tonne over LME cash prices on a CIF basis remained unchanged from last week.
